items.actClause: AN ACT to amend the county law, in relation to community and economic vitality, nutrition and healthy families, and 4-H/youth development under a form of organization and administration approved by Cornell university
items.memo:
BILL NUMBER:S4240

TITLE OF BILL:  An act to amend the county law, in relation to
community and economic vitality, nutrition and healthy families, and
4-H/youth development under a form of organization and administration
approved by Cornell university

PURPOSE:

To amend the county law pursuant to statutory authority governing
Cornell Cooperative Extension and to best reflect some of the
technical practices or programs like 4-H, occurring within the
Extension System.

SUMMARY OF PROVISIONS:

Section one amends paragraph (b) of subdivision 8 of § 224 of the
County Law to replace the terms, "home economics and community
betterment," with "community and economic vitality, nutrition and
health families, and 4-H/youth development."

Section two amends paragraph (d) of subdivision 8 of § 224 of the
County Law to provide that additional state allocations shall be
distributed to the county associations in a percentage proportionate
to their most recent county appropriation. Such appropriation may not
include any amount attributed to in-kind contributions, service
agreements, or contracts.

Section three amends paragraph (e) of subdivision 8 of § 224 of the
County Law by adding a new subparagraph 7 providing that in support of
its operations, research, and educational programming needs, an
association may contract with one or more entities, to provide
services, compensated or uncompensated, consistent with this section.
Such contracts are subject to review by Cornell University.

Section four provides the effective date.

JUSTIFICATION:

In 1862, the federal government through the Morrill Act established a
system whereby each state could designate a "land grant" institute of
higher education with the sole purpose of transmitting research based
knowledge and extension to the communities in the subject areas of
practical agriculture, science, military science and engineering.
Cornell University is New York State's land grant institution, and its
educational mission of "boots on the ground" in local communities is
delivered through the unique county structure of Cornell Cooperative
Extension. The Cornell Cooperative Extension system has compiled an
impressive record with 1.4 million New Yorkers served annually through
their programming in agriculture, youth development, nutrition,
renewable energy and many other areas.

The statutory authority governing Cornell Cooperative Extension,
however, is dated and does not best reflect some of the technical
practices or programs like 4-H, occurring within the Extension System.
For instance, fully clarifying that local Cooperative Extensions can
compete for mission appropriate federal grant funding would augment


Extension's work in local communities. County governments are the
primary funders of the County Extension network.  In the event that
state funding through § 224 of the County Law for the extension system
is supplemented, the current statute has no mechanism to distribute
any additional resources without requiring cash strapped local
governments to increase local appropriations.  This means additional
state dollars in the system could not actually be utilized in the
local communities. Updating the law to reflect the mission of Cornell
Cooperative Extension in community betterment and 4-H, as well as
making some technical changes would greatly assist the Extension
System to keep meeting the needs of New Yorkers now and in the future.

LEGISLATIVE HISTORY:

New bill.

FISCAL IMPLICATIONS:

None.

EFFECTIVE DATE:

This act shall take effect immediately.
